For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the cereal Bars came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cereal-bars" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cereal-bars-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of cereal bars, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Cereal Bars FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cereal-bars" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cereal-bars" data-question="What heavy metals are found in cereal Bars?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in cereal Bars?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium and uranium in cereal Bars, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Spungen JH, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Infants&#39; and young children&#39;s dietary exposures to lead and cadmium: FDA total diet study 2018-2020</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA, Arcella D, Cascio C, Gómez Ruiz JA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Chronic dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in cereal Bars, as sold from 39 results in 2 reporting regions, with subgroup medians below 43 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cereal-bars" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cereal-bars" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in cereal Bars?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in cereal Bars?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, cereal Bars, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EURO (15.1 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (18.5 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cereal-bars-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cereal-bars-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in cereal Bars is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in cereal Bars is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA, Arcella D, Cascio C, Gómez Ruiz JA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Chronic dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Across 2 other studies of ordinary farms and markets, reported inorganic arsenic means and medians with the basis not stated ranged from 4 µg/kg (EFSA 2021) to 21 µg/kg (EFSA 2021).<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2021-chronic-exposure-iAs|4]]<span
